# std::differential

<!-- Generated by scripts/check_spec.py from docs/spec/std-differential.toml. Edit that file and run `python3 scripts/check_spec.py --write`. -->

The laws of the metric-free cotangent pullback of `std::differential`, from ADR 0001 §10. For a smooth map f, a point x and a seed η over f(x), the pullback is the covector η ∘ Df(x) over x. A seed over another point gives the failure value ⊥. The theorems below concern the runtime operations that the `std::differential` bindings evaluate to. The kernel compiles each reverse pass that it can read into generated Core, which calls these operations only for its opaque steps; [compiled reverse Core](reverse-core.md) states what that Core computes. The runtime operations remain the reference that it agrees with.

[Specifications](../specifications.md) defines the [claim statuses](../specifications.md#claim-statuses) and the checks. This chapter is generated from [`docs/spec/std-differential.toml`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/docs/spec/std-differential.toml).

<a id="differential.pullback.linear"></a>

## Linearity in the seed

- Property: `differential.pullback.linear`
- Subject: `std::differential::pullback`
- Rule: [ADR 0001 §10, Laws](../adr/0001-mathematics-first-stdlib.md#laws)

Let f be a smooth map, x a point, η and η' seeds over f(x), and a and b rationals. The pullback along f at x is linear in the seed: it maps aη + bη' to a times the pullback of η plus b times the pullback of η'.

- Example: Along f(t) = (t, t²) at 3, the seeds (1, 0) and (0, 1) pull back to 1 dt and 6 dt, so the seed (2, 1) pulls back to 8 dt.
- Not executed: No test pulls back a combination of seeds.

Claims:

- `proof`: [Planned](../specifications.md#planned)
  - Issue: [#649](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/issues/649)
  - Note: `VastitasBridge.Differential.pullback_getD_eq_fderiv_adjoint` gives component j of the result as Σᵢ ηᵢ (Df(x) eⱼ)ᵢ, which is linear in η, but no theorem states linearity. The Python reference checks the homogeneity of its own pullback in `scripts/test_metric_reference.py`; that test does not run the kernel.

<a id="differential.pullback.identity"></a>

## Identity

- Property: `differential.pullback.identity`
- Subject: `std::differential::pullback`
- Rule: [ADR 0001 §10, Laws](../adr/0001-mathematics-first-stdlib.md#laws)

Pullback along the identity map of ℝⁿ at a point x returns every seed over x unchanged, in the `saved` and in the `recomputed` mode.

- Example: The identity of the plane pulls the covector (5, 7) at (1, 2) back to itself.
- Run by: `smooth_example_checks_builds_and_executes` in [`tests/smooth_differential.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/smooth_differential.rs)

Claims:

- `oracle`: [Proved (oracle)](../specifications.md#proved-oracle)
  - Evidence:
    - [`VastitasOracle.SmoothRuntime`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/lean/VastitasOracle/SmoothRuntime.lean): `VastitasOracle.SmoothRuntime.pullback_identity`, `VastitasOracle.SmoothRuntime.cot_identity`
    - [`VastitasOracle.SmoothCalculus`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/lean/VastitasOracle/SmoothCalculus.lean): `VastitasOracle.SmoothCalculus.Cov.pullback_id`
  - Premises:
    - for `pullback_identity`: the seed lies over the point and has one component per coordinate of the point
    - for `cot_identity`: the seed has n components
- `test`: [Tested](../specifications.md#tested)
  - Evidence:
    - `smooth_example_checks_builds_and_executes` in [`tests/smooth_differential.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/smooth_differential.rs)
    - `mutated_observations_change_the_native_result` in [`tests/smooth_differential.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/smooth_differential.rs)
  - Note: Observation 15 of the [acceptance example](../stage3-acceptance.md#acceptance-conditions) pulls a covector back along the identity of the plane. Observation 10 pulls the failure value back along the identity of the line. The mutation test shows that a wrong result changes the native output.
- `native`: [Not claimed](../specifications.md#not-claimed)
  - Reason: The theorems concern the Lean runtime definitions that the checker shares with the generated programs, which call them for opaque steps and for reverse passes that the compilation keeps. A compiled reverse pass runs generated Core, whose agreement with these definitions is proved per site under premises and tested on whole programs ([compiled reverse Core](reverse-core.md)). No claim states that the compiled native code refines them. Tests run the native code.

<a id="differential.pullback.composition"></a>

## Composition

- Property: `differential.pullback.composition`
- Subject: `std::differential::pullback`
- Rule: [ADR 0001 §10, Laws](../adr/0001-mathematics-first-stdlib.md#laws)

Pullback along g ∘ f at x equals pullback along g at f(x) followed by pullback along f at x. This holds for every seed, including a seed over another point and the failure value ⊥.

- Example: Take f(t) = (t, t²) and g(x, y) = x² + y. The seed dt at g(f(3)) = 18 pulls back along g at (3, 9), then along f at 3, to 12 dt. That is its pullback along g ∘ f at 3.
- Run by: `library_profile_checks_builds_and_runs_from_a_path_package` in [`tests/stdlib_differential.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/stdlib_differential.rs)

Claims:

- `oracle`: [Proved (oracle)](../specifications.md#proved-oracle)
  - Evidence:
    - [`VastitasOracle.SmoothRuntime`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/lean/VastitasOracle/SmoothRuntime.lean): `VastitasOracle.SmoothRuntime.pullback_stepwise`, `VastitasOracle.SmoothRuntime.pullback_stepwise_of_wellTyped`
    - [`VastitasOracle.SmoothCalculus`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/lean/VastitasOracle/SmoothCalculus.lean): `VastitasOracle.SmoothCalculus.cot_compose`, `VastitasOracle.SmoothCalculus.backward_eq_cot`, `VastitasOracle.SmoothCalculus.pullback_composite`, `VastitasOracle.SmoothCalculus.Cov.pullback_comp`
  - Premises:
    - for `pullback_stepwise`: the input arity of the outer program equals the output arity of the inner one; `pullback_stepwise_of_wellTyped` derives this from the typing of the composite
    - for `cot_compose`: both maps are well formed between their dimensions
    - for `backward_eq_cot` and `pullback_composite`: the program is well typed
  - Note: `pullback_stepwise` states the law for the program node that `compose` builds. `backward_eq_cot` and `pullback_composite` show that this pullback equals the pullback along the composite polynomial map, and `cot_compose` is the chain rule for that map. The chain-rule proofs of `SmoothCalculus` use dual numbers and `Lean.Grind.CommRing`, not mathlib.
- `bridge`: [Proved (bridge)](../specifications.md#proved-bridge)
  - Evidence:
    - [`VastitasBridge.Differential.ChainRule`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/lean-bridge/VastitasBridge/Differential/ChainRule.lean): `VastitasBridge.Differential.cot_compose`, `VastitasBridge.Differential.backward_eq_cot`, `VastitasBridge.Differential.pullback_composite`, `VastitasBridge.Differential.pullback_comp`
    - [`VastitasBridge.Differential.Kaehler`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/lean-bridge/VastitasBridge/Differential/Kaehler.lean): `VastitasBridge.Differential.cot_compose_kaehler`
  - Premises:
    - for `cot_compose`, `pullback_comp` and `cot_compose_kaehler`: both maps are well formed between their dimensions
    - for `backward_eq_cot` and `pullback_composite`: the program is well typed
  - Assumes: [mathlib](assumptions.md#assumption.mathlib)
  - Note: `cot_compose` follows the formal chain rule `pderiv_aeval` for mathlib's `pderiv`, which `VastitasBridge.Differential.Prerequisites` proves. `cot_compose_kaehler` proves the same equation from the functoriality of Kähler differentials, independently of `cot_compose`.
- `test`: [Tested](../specifications.md#tested)
  - Evidence:
    - `smooth_example_checks_builds_and_executes` in [`tests/smooth_differential.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/smooth_differential.rs)
    - `mutated_observations_change_the_native_result` in [`tests/smooth_differential.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/smooth_differential.rs)
    - `library_profile_checks_builds_and_runs_from_a_path_package` in [`tests/stdlib_differential.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/stdlib_differential.rs)
    - [`VastitasAlgebraTest.SmoothReferenceRegression`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/lean-kernel/VastitasAlgebraTest/SmoothReferenceRegression.lean), built by [`scripts/check_kernel_regressions.sh`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/scripts/check_kernel_regressions.sh)
  - Note: Observation 1 of the [acceptance example](../stage3-acceptance.md#acceptance-conditions) checks 12 dt. Observations 2 to 4 compare the stepwise pullback with the pullback along the composite program, along the composite as one map and along a declared map. Observation 5 checks that the composite and the declared map are the same map. Since the reverse passes are compiled, both sides of observation 2 run Jacobian steps along `g` and `f`, and so do both sides of the composition observation of the library package, so neither runs the runtime pass on a composite program. Observation 3 compares the stepwise pullback with the runtime pass along the composite as one map, an opaque step over `composite(…)`, and observation 4 with the table of the declared map `gf`. `SmoothReferenceRegression` runs the runtime pass on the composite programs of `tests/fixtures/smooth-differential.json`, which the independent Python references generate.
- `native`: [Not claimed](../specifications.md#not-claimed)
  - Reason: The theorems concern the Lean runtime definitions that the checker shares with the generated programs, which call them for opaque steps and for reverse passes that the compilation keeps. A compiled reverse pass runs generated Core, whose agreement with these definitions is proved per site under premises and tested on whole programs ([compiled reverse Core](reverse-core.md)). No claim states that the compiled native code refines them. Tests run the native code.
